page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.32-512 is a flexible virtual machine instance configured with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs powered by the AMD EPYC 9J14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture and operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz with dedicated CPU allocation, it features simultaneous multithreading with two threads per physical core. The instance provides 512 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation that aligns directly with memory-intensive compute requirements.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, operating with zero GPUs. As a result, all persistent file systems and transactional data stores rely on attached cloud network block storage. Networking capabilities include one complimentary public IPv4 address for external connectivity.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the flexible resource configuration allows memory capacity to scale independently to match large workloads without forcing oversized core allocations. The balanced high-density memory footprint reduces unnecessary virtual socket overhead in enterprise deployments. This profile is engineered for memory-heavy enterprise software, in-memory caching solutions, enterprise resource planning systems, large relational databases, and multi-threaded analytical processing pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.32-512 is an enterprise virtual machine instance powered by a 2.3 GHz AMD EPYC 9J14 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 physical cores, 64 vCPUs via two threads per core, and dedicated CPU allocation alongside 512 GB of system RAM. This delivers an 8 GB per vCPU memory profile suitable for large in-memory footprints. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and features no integrated GPU hardware or local NVMe storage, directing persistent I/O workloads to external block storage volumes. By offering a high ratio of memory to compute cores, VM.Standard.E5.Flex.32-512 provides cost-effective resource consolidation for memory-intensive architectures. It is well-fitted for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching, distributed analytics, and memory-constrained enterprise applications.
